text:
lina: :rotating_light: paging SRE - spike in 5xx/timeouts for inference-gateway, started ~11:08 UTC. Errors across multiple customer routes. Auto-alerts from incident-bot.

incident-bot: alert triggered: HIGH error-rate on /v1/generate (5xx > 8% over 5m). Pager: @pagerduty oncall.

omar: jumping in. seeing a large backlog in the batching scheduler queues. Q depth per-worker: 1200 -> 4000 over 10m. head-of-line latencies spiking.

ryan: confirmed from logs: lots of kvcache misses followed by long tail token latencies. gateway timeouts returning 504s.

lina: customer impact? any users getting errors or just latency?

omar: both. small % of requests timeout at gateway (504). Upstream returns 5xx for long-running batches. Surface metrics show increase in per-request service time and queue wait.

ryan: stack traces attached in logs:
```
2026-02-18T11:12:05Z ERROR scheduler: batch exec exceeded timeout after 30s; callers: 127
2026-02-18T11:12:05Z WARN gateway: upstream 502 from model-worker-23
```

lina: initial mitigation idea: 1) throttle incoming rate from gateway to avoid new long-run batches 2) open failover route to smaller model variant 3) evict stuck batches older than Xs.

omar: agree. Also increase scheduler workers to drain queue while rolling evictions. I'll start scaling worker pool by +30% on Dedicated pool.

ryan: I'll flip a routing policy to route non-critical tenant traffic to the smaller-quantized model (redwood-model-lite) and drop batch size for that route. Command:
```
# console CLI
redwood route update --route /v1/generate --policy fallback=redwood-model-lite --max-batch-size 8
```

lina: do that for test tenants first. We don't want config typos to affect everyone. Can you patch canary group now?

ryan: done on canary (10% traffic). Seeing error rate drop there to 1.2%. Good sign.

omar: scaling started. kube scale workerDeployment --replicas=26 (was 20).

devops-bot: deploy triggered: workerDeployment -> replicas=26 by omar at 11:20 UTC.

lina: we're still seeing HOL (head-of-line) blocking: a few very large requests stuck at front of queue preventing smaller batches from being processed. Need immediate eviction policy.

omar: I can enable the short-lived-ejector: evict any queued item > 8s wait and requeue with lower priority. Applying now.

omar: applying config patch:
```
PATCH /configs/scheduler
{
  "evict_threshold_ms": 8000,
  "requeue_priority":"low",
  "max_requeues":1
}
```

incident-bot: config change logged and rolled out to 8/12 scheduler shards.

ryan: once shards roll we should watch for request trims causing higher upstream retries. Also coordinate with gateway to increase 504 timeout to 60s temporarily while we drain.

lina: agreed. gateway timeout to 60s for affected route only. omar, can you patch?

omar: patched gateway route timeout: 30s -> 60s for /v1/generate on region-us-east.

pagerduty: paging status updated: acknowledgement by omar. escalation halted.

lina: customer-facing comms: drafting DM to top-5 impacted customers: explain we're mitigating and offering priority reroute to dedicated low-latency pool.

ryan: metrics after actions (11:30 UTC):
- scheduler queue depth: 4000 -> 900 (draining)
- 5xx rate global: 8.4% -> 2.1%
- gateway 504 count: 120/min -> 15/min

omar: eviction causing some requests to be retried but overall throughput improved. continuing scale for another 10m.

lina: postmortem notes to capture: root cause likely surge of long-sequence requests + a recent batching-config change that increased max-batch-size to 256 two days ago. That config allowed very long batches to form and amplified HOL blocking when combined with a KV-cache miss pattern.

ryan: saving relevant logs to S3: s3://redwood-incident-logs/1769456789/*.gz

omar: rolling back the max-batch-size experiment to 128 on non-dedicated routes. Command:
```
redwood config set --service scheduler --max-batch-size 128 --scope=shared
```
devops-bot: config change queued and rolled out to 12/12 scheduler shards.

lina: good. let's keep the fallback policy in place for 1h, watch for regressions. Who's owning next 30m watch?

omar: I'll stay on primary and hand off to ryan at 12:00 UTC.

ryan: taking handoff at 12:00 UTC. I'll monitor SLIs and customer DMs.

lina: summary for incident log: cause = batching config + sudden traffic spike + KV cache miss pattern -> HOL queueing -> worker starvation -> increased worker-side timeouts -> gateway 504/502s; mitigations = scale workers, enable eviction, increase route timeout, fallback to smaller model, rollback batch-size experiment, canary routing, customer communication.

incident-bot: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. created incident ticket INC-2026-2450.

lina: assigning postmortem to eng-runtime; deadline for draft = 2026-02-21. Add action items: revert risky experiments with rollback playbook, add automatic HOL eviction earlier, alert for batch size distribution skew, and add circuit-breaker to push to fallback model when queue depth > threshold.

omar: noted. I'll add a follow-up PR for eviction tuning and a dashboard panel for queue age distribution.

ryan: closing the active paging loop. will update incident ticket with timeline + metric dumps.

lina: thanks everyone. :raised_hands:

pagerduty: incident acknowledged and set to status: monitoring by omar.

(END THREAD)
